sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the
record.

2. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in case no.5451 of 2021, case
crime No.128 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station
Bilsi, District Budaun with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
3.  It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
The applicant is husband of deceased and their marriage has taken place about six years prior to the incident.
After marriage, during period of six years, there was no complaint of any dowry demand and harassment of deceased.

The allegations Dinesh vs State Of U.P. on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6539261/
1 that deceased was being harassed on account of dowry demand, are thoroughly false.

It was submitted that in fact an scuffle has taken place on 01.04.2020 between the family of applicant and his neighbourers and in that scuffle the deceased has sustained some internal injuries and later on,
she died.
Regarding said incident, a news was also published in the news paper.
After death of deceased, the mother of applicant has given information to the police, regarding which a general diary entry was recorded at police station.

In postmortem report of deceased, no external injury has been shown on the body of deceased, however, it was shown that liver of deceased was lacerated and cause of death is ante-mortem injury to vital organ.

After death of deceased, an information was given to the parental family of deceased and at the time of inquest proceedings on 02.04.2020 the brother and other family members of deceased were present and they are also witnesses at the inquest report.
The applicant and his family members were also present but at that time, no report was lodged.

After about two months of the alleged incident, the informant has lodged first information report of this case on 28.05.2020., making false and baseless allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased.
It is further submitted that applicant has already undergone the custody of three years.

Lastly, it has been submitted that the applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 29.05.2020, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant-accused is husband of deceased, who has suffered unnatural death within a period of six years from her marriage.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant-accused Dinesh involved in aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
(i) The applicant-accused shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant-accused shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant-accused shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant-accused shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant-accused shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement,
threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant-accused in accordance with law.
